look_here_first: Look FIRST at the mature UPPER leaf attachment: thick, stiff, strongly HEART-SHAPED-CLASPING to auriculate leaf bases with flat margins. Inflorescence side branches often emerge almost horizontally before curving up. Compare S. oblongifolium's shorter oblong leaves and bushier branching. Important: S. patens var. patens can have DENSE stalked glands on phyllaries, so a glandular photo alone cannot identify S. oblongifolium.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Against S. oblongifolium: look at how strongly upper leaves clasp the stem—S. patens upper leaves are truly cordate-amplexicaul/auriculate, whereas S. oblongifolium has relatively short oblong leaves that are often only rounded or mildly clasping. Glandular phyllaries occur in S. patens too, with substantial varietal variation; gland presence is NOT an exclusive oblongifolium character.
